discovery.hypothesis: Covers reports Daniels' rushing line jumped from 31.5 to 39.5 after one 103-yard game on just nine carries, two of them long TD runs. That move may overweight a single high-variance result. A disciplined 49ers zone defense that gives up few explosive plays, plus the injury risk to his elbow, could hold him under the higher line.
discovery.question: Is Washington actually calling more designed runs for Daniels, beyond scrambles, now that its RB room is banged up? And is the current line still near 39.5?

Game status | Jacory Croskey-Merritt ruled out vs. 49ers
NFL Week 6 odds, predictions, expert picks: Cowboys roll into Lambeau Field to face Packers

findings.note: The 49ers ruled out WR Deebo Samuel, DL Nick Bosa, LB Garret Wallow and S Marques Sigle. WR Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles, no practice all week), WR Christian Kirk, CB Upton Stout and DL Mykel Williams are questionable, which weakens a team laying 7.5 points.

Washington ruled out leading rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin), OLB Jean-Baptiste, DE Omenihu and backup QB Mariota. WR Diggs and several safeties are questionable, while QB Jayden Daniels practiced fully all week.
The 49ers' game page shows Washington at 1-3-1 and San Francisco unbeaten at 5-0 after a 32-29 win over Seattle. The Monday night game at Levi's Stadium kicks off at 5:15 PM PDT.

Washington's leading rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt (239 yards, 2 TDs) is out Monday after reinjuring his groin, so the Commanders will lean on Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler, who were both limited in practice with shoulder and chest issues.

SF ruled out DE Nick Bosa (calf), WR Deebo Samuel, S Marques Sigle and LB Garret Wallow and listed Mike Evans and Christian Kirk as questionable. On the other side, FB Kyle Juszczyk and DT James Thompson Jr. return for SF.

Washington's own site calls SF undefeated so far, a tough matchup. Jayden Daniels returned last week from a dislocated elbow and practiced fully all week, but Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is questionable and Washington is coming off a 27-27 tie with the Giants.

Josh Inglis of Covers picks Under 52.5, which is half a point better than our 52. He cites injuries to key offensive players on both teams, including Deebo Samuel being out, Mike Evans not practicing Friday, and the 49ers possibly using WR8 and WR9.

A Covers props writer picks Brock Purdy over 249.5 passing yards and a George Kittle touchdown. The writer says Washington allows the fourth-most passing yards (255 per game), is tied for the most passing TDs allowed (14), and has thin safety depth.

The 49ers ruled out Nick Bosa, which may weaken their pass rush, as well as Deebo Samuel, safety Marques Sigle and LB Garret Wallow. Mike Evans (Achilles soreness, no practice) is questionable, Christian Kirk could possibly come back from IR, and Kyle Juszczyk will play.
ESPN lists 1,196 passing yards for Purdy over 5 games, about 239 per game and well under 261.5, and says he threw for only 189 yards on 19-of-29 passing in last week's win over Seattle.

CBS writer John Breech picks the 49ers -7.5 and 34-20, saying Washington has given up the fourth-most passing yards; the game opened at 49ers -7.5, O/U 50.5, so a lopsided score could cut late passing. This is a side pick, not a pick on Purdy's yards.
Commanders' team site says the 49ers will be without Deebo Samuel, who has 3 receiving TDs. It also says Mike Evans has been Purdy's reliable top target and Purdy had been sacked only three times.
